name: Mental Health Dialogue Safety Benchmark
description: Dialogue safety remains a pervasive challenge in open-domain human-machine interaction. Existing approaches propose distinctive dialogue safety taxonomies and datasets for detecting explicitly harmful responses. However, these taxonomies may not be suitable for analyzing response safety in mental health support. In real-world interactions, a model response deemed acceptable in casual conversations might have a negligible positive impact on users seeking mental health support. To address these limitations, this paper aims to develop a theoretically and factually grounded taxonomy that prioritizes the positive impact on help-seekers. Additionally, we create a benchmark corpus with fine-grained labels for each dialogue session to facilitate further research. We analyze the dataset using popular language models, including BERT-base, RoBERTa-large, and ChatGPT, to detect and understand unsafe responses within the context of mental health support.
